ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure A, this is a graph of an alternating voltage varying with time. In each cycle, during the first half of the cycle the voltage is constant, and during the second half of the cycle the voltage varies according to a sine law. If this alternating current is connected into the circuit shown in Figure B, and the resistance of resistor R is 100 Ω, what is the reading of the ideal ammeter?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the graph: Figure A is a graph of voltage u varying with time t, with the vertical axis labeled u/V and the horizontal axis labeled t/(×10^-2 s). It can be seen from the graph that, in each cycle, the voltage in the first half is a constant +100 V; the voltage in the second half varies below the 0 axis according to a half sine curve, with the lowest point 50 V below the 0 axis, so it can be regarded as a negative half sine wave with amplitude 50 V. In Figure B, the alternating current source is connected into the circuit, the ideal ammeter A is connected in series with resistor R, the voltmeter V is connected in parallel across the two ends of the power source, and the problem gives R=100 Ω. Then reason: the reading of the ideal ammeter is the effective value of the alternating current. First find the effective value of this alternating voltage. Let the period be T. In the first T/2, u=100 V, so the contribution of this part to the mean square value is (1/2)×100^2. In the second T/2, it is a half sine wave with amplitude 50 V. The average value of the square of a sinusoidal quantity over half a cycle is half the square of the amplitude, so the contribution of this part to the mean square value is (1/2)×(50^2/2). Therefore U_eff^2=(1/2)·100^2+(1/2)·(50^2/2)=5000+625=5625, U_eff=75 V. The resistor is a pure resistor, so the effective value of current is I=U_eff/R=75/100=0.75 A.
